name: The Double Eagle: Habsburgs and the Holy Roman Empire
description: A family from the Alps came to rule much of Europe. This is the story of emperors, wars of religion, Vienna's music and the empire that fell in 1918.

checkpoints.name: Crown of the Romans
checkpoints.note: Charlemagne's empire was the model for the Holy Roman Empire, traditionally dated from 962. Over the centuries a family called Habsburg rose, and the lands of Hungary and Bohemia came to be tied to their crown.

checkpoints.name: Reformation and war
checkpoints.note: Martin Luther's protest began the Protestant Reformation while Charles V ruled. The Dutch Revolt and the Thirty Years' War followed, with Gustavus Adolphus on the Protestant side, and the Peace of Westphalia ended the fighting.

checkpoints.name: From Turkish siege to enlightenment
checkpoints.note: In 1683 an Ottoman army besieged Vienna and was beaten at the Battle of Vienna. Maria Theresa then ruled the Habsburg lands, with her thaler used as a coin, while Frederick the Great of Prussia became her chief rival. Mozart lived in Vienna.

checkpoints.name: Napoleon and after
checkpoints.note: The wars of the French Revolution and Napoleon shook the empire. Austerlitz was a defeat in 1805, the Holy Roman Empire ended in 1806, and the Austrian Empire took its place. The Congress of Vienna redrew the map, and 1848 brought revolutions.

checkpoints.name: The Dual Monarchy
checkpoints.note: Austria-Hungary was created in 1867 after Prussia, led by Bismarck, had defeated Austria. Vienna was the home of Klimt and Mahler. The assassination of Franz Ferdinand in 1914 led to World War I, and the empire broke up in 1918.
